title: Seeing the footprints
hook: picture two: tracks, found in the teachings (Ox-Herding 2)
tomorrow: what did one pebble hitting bamboo show a monk?

segments.voice: Yesterday, searching: a herder alone in the grass, looking for an ox the preface says was never lost. Picture two.

A map app shows a blue line, never the street itself. Hold that thought. Zen has a saying, credited by tradition to Bodhidharma: a special transmission outside the scriptures, not depending on words. So here's the odd detail in Kuoan's second picture. How does the herder find the first tracks of his ox? The preface says it plainly: with the help of the sutras, by asking into the teachings. A school that says don't depend on words sends its searcher straight to the books. Why would it do that?
screen: `A BLUE LINE, NOT THE STREET.` → `OUTSIDE THE SCRIPTURES?` → `HE FINDS TRACKS IN THE SUTRAS.`

segments.voice: Look closely at what he finds. Not the ox. Footprints. Kuoan's verse scatters them by the water and under the trees, all through the fragrant grass. The preface says that through the teachings he starts to understand that vessels, however many, are made of the same gold, and that all things are part of his own self. Then it adds a warning: he can't yet tell true from false. He hasn't entered the gate. He has only seen the tracks. That solves the puzzle. Zen doesn't throw the books away; it puts them in their place. A teaching is a footprint: real, made by the ox, worth following, and not the ox. There's an old Buddhist image for the same thing, from the Lankavatara Sutra: a finger pointing at the moon. Follow the finger, but don't stare at it. Then Kuoan adds a lovely line: even in the deepest mountains, the ox's nose reaches the sky. The tracks lead somewhere that can't stay hidden. The teachers on this path have worked like that all along. Marcus, Rumi, Zhuangzi, Julian of Norwich: footprints, every one of them, pointing past themselves.
screen: `NOT THE OX: FOOTPRINTS.` · `HE CAN'T YET TELL TRUE FROM FALSE.` · `A FINGER POINTING AT THE MOON.` · `ITS NOSE REACHES THE SKY.` · then, large: `THE FOOTPRINTS.`

segments.voice: Name, out loud and softly, three teachings that gave you tracks on this path: a line, a story, a practice. After each one, add one word: footprint. Then sit the rest of the two minutes with the tracks behind you and the hill still ahead.
Seeing the footprints: Kuoan's second picture. The tracks are found in the teachings; they point to the ox and aren't the ox.
Hold onto this: the footprints, real tracks worth following, and still not the ox. That's picture two.

screen: `DAY 1780 COUNTS.` → `OX-HERDING · PICTURE 2 OF 10.` → `THE SUMMIT · 4 OF 15.` → `TOMORROW: WHAT DID A PEBBLE ON BAMBOO SHOW A MONK?`

howItsDone: Zen communities chant and study sutras alongside sitting; teachers often point to the image of a finger pointing at the moon. People on this path keep their teachers' lines as tracks, not as the destination.

fork.setup: a coworker has read every book on mindfulness and says he's 'basically got it,' though he's never sat once. what would picture two say?
options: he's found real footprints, but not the ox yet.
reading that much is the ox itself; he's done.
the books were a waste; Zen says never to read.
fork.reveal: Kuoan's herder finds tracks through the teachings, then admits he hasn't entered the gate. the footprints are real and worth following, and they point past themselves.
